chunks: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar asked him, and he said:

He said to him: May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men, among whom she has no mahram, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her?

He said: “Of her, only that which Allah has made tayammum obligatory upon them for is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her features that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded to be covered to be uncovered.”
He said to him: How is that to be done with her? He said: “The inner side of her hands is washed, then her face is washed, then the outer side of her hands is washed.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution; here, the body parts corresponding to it
key_terms.بَاطِنُ كَفَّيْهَا: the inner sides of her hands
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative within the prohibited degrees of marriage
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: her bodily features or attractions that must remain covered

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies while traveling with non-mahram men and no women are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for handling the body of a deceased woman who dies while traveling among unrelated men and in the absence of other women. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that only the parts associated with tayammum are to be washed, while preserving her bodily covering and avoiding touch or uncovering what Allah has commanded to be concealed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.435 - Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asked Imam Al-Sadiq (as):
"May I be your ransom, what is your ruling about a woman who dies while traveling with men, none of whom are her mahram (close relatives), and no women are present? What should be done with her?"

Imam (as) replied: "Only those parts that Allah (swt) has required for tayammum (dry ablution) should be washed, and She should not be touched or any of her private features, which Allah (swt) has commanded to be covered, uncovered."

He then asked: "How should it be done?"
Imam (as) replied: "Her inner palms should be washed first, then her face, followed by washing the backs of her hands”.
